name: Mint
grown_as: Garden mint (spearmint), a hardy perennial that spreads by runners and is often kept in a pot. The library also lists Applemint, a different mint with round, soft, woolly leaves. Drawn here as spearmint. ⚠️ CHECK which mint William grows, or whether two drawings are wanted.
habit: A spreading patch of upright, unbranched or little-branched square stems 30 to 80 cm high, rising from white or pale runners just under or along the soil surface.

leaf.arrangement: Opposite, in pairs, each pair at right angles to the one below
leaf.outline: Lance-shaped, long and narrow, 4 to 9 cm long and 1.5 to 3 cm wide, widest near the base
leaf.margin: Sharp, forward-pointing, irregular saw teeth along almost the whole edge, from near the base to the tip
leaf.veins: A midrib and 5 to 8 side veins each side, pressed in so the leaf looks wrinkled
leaf.surface: Smooth or almost so, matt to slightly shiny, wrinkled
leaf.stalk: None or almost none: the leaf sits right on the stem

flower.petals: Joined; four nearly equal lobes, the top one a little broader
flower.colour: Pale lilac to pink, sometimes white
flower.centre: Four stamens sticking out beyond the petals
flower.behind: A small green bell-shaped calyx with five narrow teeth
flower.carried: In many crowded rings that make a slender, tapering, upright spike 3 to 10 cm long at the top of each stem, the lower rings a little apart; smaller spikes from the upper leaf joints
flower.size: About 3 mm long; the spike about 1 cm thick

fruit: Rarely sets seed; the spikes dry brown with tiny nutlets in the calyces.
seedling: Not drawn: grown from runners or bought plants.
winter: Dies down to the ground. Runners lie at or just under the surface, sometimes with a few small leafy shoots showing in mild winters.

leaf: a long narrow lance-shaped leaf, much longer than wide
sharp saw teeth along almost the whole edge
bloom: a slender tapering spike made of many crowded rings of tiny flowers
flowers pale lilac with stamens sticking out
young: upright square stems with narrow stalkless leaves in opposite pairs
shoots rising from runners, not a single crown
crop: a dense patch of upright stems thick with narrow toothed stalkless leaves
each pair of leaves at right angles to the next
flower: slender pale lilac spikes at the stem tops
narrow toothed leaves in pairs below
seedhead: dry brown slender spikes on the old stems
dormant: bare soil with pale runners at the surface
a few small shoots or none

look_alikes: Applemint has round, soft, grey-woolly leaves. Peppermint has darker leaves on short stalks, purple-tinged stems and thicker, blunter spikes. Water mint has stalked oval leaves and round heads of flowers. Lemon balm has broad stalked leaves with round teeth and flowers in the leaf joints.
